# CC08: 法慧寺 Fahui Si

Wave 3 · Changchun Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=CC08` · Page: `/scenes/#CC08` · Row: `research/buildings/CC08-fahui-si/`

## What it was

法慧寺 Fahui Si, a Buddhist temple on the south slope of the ridge north of 海岳开襟, west of 宝相寺 (S05 j83:12a; E0171, E0173). 日下旧闻考: gate facing west (plaque 普香界), the 四面延楼, the rear hall 光明性海, and in a west court a glazed square pagoda (S05 j83:12a: 其西别院有琉璃方塔). Finished 1747; S361 gives a five-bay main hall, a five-bay rear-facing tower with eleven-bay wings (the 四面延楼), and the pagoda as seven tiers, square below and round above, 23.55 m high (E0174). The use of eunuchs as monks here ended in 1839 (E1261, E0173). The emperor visited in 1856 (E1524). Not among the buildings left standing after 1860 (E0451, after 刘敦桢), so it burned in October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188); the glazed pagoda stood until 1900 according to an old man Malone spoke to (E0172).

From the inventory row: **built** 1747; **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S47, S01, S361).

## Gaps and wishlist

The pagoda is the only tall form of this part of the garden; its height 23.55 m (S361) has no stated basis on disk. R0323 cites an NLC elevation 法慧寺琉璃塔立样图: not viewed. The temple plan 样069-1 (E0175) is not viewed. No pre-1900 photograph of the pagoda found.
